blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten and name the rules. Skip empty emails with an early `continue` (`if row.email.is_empty() { continue; }`). Extract the seat loop, which is duplicated in the `Some` and `None` arms (lines 19-26 and 31-36), into one helper such as `add_new_seats(db, account_id, &row.seats, &existing_seats) -> Result<usize, DbError>` that filters with `.filter(|s| !existing.contains(s)).filter(|s| is_seat_email(s))`. Give the two bare filters a name or a comment saying why: `seat.contains('@')` (line 21, 32) — a reader cannot tell whether it validates an email or drops some other kind of seat — and `account.plan != row.plan` (line 18), which means an existing account gets its new seats only when the CSV's plan differs from the stored one and is otherwise silently skipped; a newcomer reads it as inverted and cannot answer why without the plan, which does not say either. Note also that the plan itself is never updated in that branch, so the condition reads like a missing step. The doc comment "returns how many seats were created" should say that seats of unchanged-plan accounts and seats without `@` are skipped.
findings.title: `import` nests five levels deep and hides its rules in unexplained filters
